title: Cardiac Tamponade: Etiology, Therapy and Outcomes
summary:
Cardiac tamponade is a life-threatening emergency. It leads to an increase in intrapericardial pressure, resulting in compression of the heart. This ultimately impairs hemodynamics and can cause obstructive shock, cardiac arrest, and death. Accordingly, cardiac tamponade requires prompt diagnosis and timely treatment. Due to the diverse underlying causes (e.g. traumatic, malignant, infectious), a tailored therapeutic approach is necessary.

Using retrospective data from the Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin, this study investigates the causes (etiology) of cardiac tamponade, evaluates the therapeutic approaches applied (therapy), and analyzes the resulting clinical outcomes (outcome) in order to identify associations between etiology, treatment, and patient course, and to optimize care.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of patients who were treated for cardiac tamponade at Charité - Universitätsmedizin between 1st of January 2023 and 31st of December 2025.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients treated at Charité - Universitätsmedizin for cardiac tamponade between 1st of January 2023 and 31st of December 2025
- Adults only, of all sexes
- Patient data must be complete to allow analysis of the research question
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients with cardiac tamponade and incomplete data (e.g. laboratory results or imaging findings) that prevent determination of the underlying etiology of the tamponade
- Patients with cardiac tamponade and incomplete documentation of therapy and mortality
